speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry will consider requiring manufacturers of health supplements to provide test results from accredited laboratories to back up their advertising claims in order to prevent inaccurate representation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
text: When detected, these advertisers will be ordered to stop the publication of these advertisements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition, HSA also educates the public to be cautious of exaggerated advertising claims through consumer advisories.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I want to thank the Senior Minister of State for his response.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, since HSA already has guidelines, would the Ministry of Health consider making sure that we do some legislation to back it up?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With regard to the issue about the test results, I understand that what HSA does now is that they actually test these supplements for toxic substances.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am not sure what the testing or monitoring regime is.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps the Senior Minister of State could enlighten the House on what some of these monitoring regimes are.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But as I understand it, they do not also test whether these supplements actually contain what they profess to contain.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, for example, if a product says "I contain X grammes of this active ingredient", do we actually know that this product actually contains X grammes of this ingredient?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because there have been many cases over the years all over the world when independent testers actually test these products, they do not actually contain the health ingredients that they say that they do.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Is it just caveat emptor or do they have some avenues they can turn to for redress?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will deal with all three of the supplementary questions together.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Health supplements, by definition, they contain minerals, usually vitamins, amino acids, and largely comprise substances that are natural from animal or plant extracts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, to that extent, when Dr Chia Shi-Lu speaks about the guidelines, there are guidelines and they are published, and Dr Chia may know that they are published for the industry's reference, and they do provide recommendations along the lines of the safety and quality standards: what ingredients are allowable and the claims that can be made about those ingredients, and also the heavy metal and microbial limits and weight of these items.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: HSA also provides guidelines on what precise information can appear on the labels to those items.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They also allow HSA to initiate timely product recalls should there be any adverse reaction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The post-market surveillance testing for health supplements is also complemented by an adverse reaction monitoring, which Dr Chia Shi-Lu also mentioned in his third supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And all that taken together allows HSA to surveil the market.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As for whether or not the consumers of these items have a recourse subsequently, obviously it is, to some extent, caveat emptor when you buy but, certainly, HSA would welcome complaints that are being made.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I mentioned, adverse reaction monitoring is being carried out.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the sense of the market, the information and intelligence gathered from the market would help HSA in making those assessments.
